pointers.sentence: The rel is what stands in the other model's list of fields, and it is what names the attribute the other class is given (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.__init__`, `django/db/models/fields/reverse_related.py:ForeignObjectRel`).

The rel is what stands in the other model's list of fields, and it is what names the attribute the other class is given (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.__init__`, `django/db/models/fields/reverse_related.py:ForeignObjectRel`).

On its own class it leaves the key under the field's attname, `"ship_id"` for a sailor, and the related object under the field's name, `"ship"`, each a descriptor (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.contribute_to_class`, `django/db/models/fields/related.py:ForeignObject.contribute_to_class`).

On its own class it leaves the key under the field's attname, `"ship_id"` for a sailor, and the related object under the field's name, `"ship"`, each a descriptor (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.contribute_to_class`, `django/db/models/fields/related.py:ForeignObject.contribute_to_class`).

On the class at the far end it ordinarily leaves one more, named by the rel: for a foreign key a manager, so that the attribute `"crew"` of a ship is not a list but a descriptor that makes, at each read, a manager whose querysets are already filtered to that ship's sailors (`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py:ReverseManyToOneDescriptor.__get__`); for a one-to-one field an object, read through a descriptor of its own.

An object, the ship of a sailor or the captain of a ship, is kept in the instance's `ModelState.fields_cache` under the relation's name; a set, the crew of a ship, is kept in the instance's `_prefetched_objects_cache`, which the related manager looks in before it sends anything (`django/db/models/base.py:ModelState`, `django/db/models/fields/mixins.py:FieldCacheMixin.set_cached_value`, `django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py:create_reverse_many_to_one_manager`).

Setting `"ship"` on a sailor sets the key under `"ship_id"` and keeps the ship in the cache; for a one-to-one relation the descriptor also keeps the instance in the cache of the object it was given, so that the relation is known from both ends (`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py:ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.__set__`).

Under `FETCH_PEERS` the mode may call the descriptor's `fetch_many` instead, which fetches, by way of `prefetch_related_objects`, the ships of those sailors made by the same run of a query that are still alive and have none in their cache; under `FETCH_RAISE` it raises `FieldFetchBlocked` (`django/db/models/fetch_modes.py`, `django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py:ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.fetch_many`).

Its `get_queryset` returns the set from `_prefetched_objects_cache` where a prefetch left one there, and otherwise a new queryset narrowed to the ship, to which it hands the ship's fetch mode for the sailors that queryset makes (`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py:create_reverse_many_to_one_manager`).
